# H2 — Close the pull queue (TRACKING.md D35-1..D35-5)

**Mission** — Close all five open pull-queue rows so doctrine amendment 2 ("no new zero-consumer package while a consumer-proven ask is open", TRACKING.md §Pull queue) stops blocking new kit work. Each row absorbs a pattern already proven in throughline, and each closes only when the throughline donor copy is *deleted* and both gates are green — extraction-done = donor-deleted, verified by `task downstream-check`. This is the north star in miniature: the kit's own claim of "we have this foundation" is checked against ground truth (a real consumer actually using it, the hand-rolled copy actually gone).

**Repos & write scope** — Writes: `/Volumes/m2ext/code/geoffmilleraz/agentic-kit` and `/Volumes/m2ext/code/geoffmilleraz/throughline` (only: `app/acquire/*`, `adapters/oauth/*`, `app/ingest/coverage.go` doc note if needed, `docs/design/29-truth-path-m16.md`, `docs/design/35-evidence-acquisition.md` status notes, **plus `vendor/**` and `vendor/modules.txt`** — see vendor re-sync deliverable). Everything else (../sextant, ../growing-gardens-bi) READ-ONLY. **There is no go.work**: throughline wires the kit via `replace github.com/geoffmilleraz/agentic-kit => ../agentic-kit` in its go.mod **plus a `vendor/` directory** — its builds resolve against `vendor/github.com/geoffmilleraz/agentic-kit`, so Stage 2 cannot compile until `go mod vendor` is re-run (precedent: TRACKING F3 "throughline gate green, vendor re-synced"). **Throughline's tree is heavily dirty** (~120 modified files: `adapters/llmclient/instrument.go`, `adapters/sqlite*`, `app/ingest/{ingest_record,pipeline}.go`, ~45 files under `surfaces/web/views/*`, surfaces/web handlers, `app/output/drafting/*`, `app/chat/service_test.go`, `app/timeline/*_test.go`, **and the vendored agentic-kit/app-kit copies themselves** — `vendor/.../foundations/*` modified, `vendor/.../instrument/budget.go` untracked). H2's target files (`app/acquire/*`, `adapters/oauth/*`, `app/ingest/coverage.go`) are clean today — verify disjointness with `git status --porcelain | grep -E 'app/acquire|adapters/oauth|app/ingest/coverage'` before touching; if any target file has become dirty, STOP and report. Because re-vendoring will overwrite/mix Geoff's unreviewed vendor diffs, the vendor re-sync must be isolated and flagged (see Deliverables and Hand-back).

## Design constraints

- stdlib-only root module (`go.mod` stays require-free); `tokenlifecycle` imports nothing beyond stdlib + sibling foundations.
- CUE owns shape: `token-lifecycle` gets schema.cue + testdata/valid.cue; authenticity schema.cue updated in the same commit as types.go (drift = bug).
- Injected clocks everywhere: `Classify`/`NextAction` take `now time.Time` as a parameter (purest seam — no stored clock); `ResumeFSM` takes the clock func like `NewFSM`.
- Org-agnostic: no "Google"/provider names in `tokenlifecycle` (throughline's `tokenResponse` Google parsing stays consumer-side); DKIM/Authentication-Results ceilings are RFC-protocol facts, not an org catalog — permitted, with the asserted-vs-verified rationale in the doc comment.
- Layering: `tokenlifecycle` sits in `foundations/security/` beside `tokenization`; kebab-dir → collapsed package name; concurrency contract paragraph in every touched package doc (`tokenlifecycle`: pure functions + value types, safe concurrently; `gatedRefiner`: safe via sync.Mutex).
- Compose with existing seams by name: `queryplanner.Refiner`, `queryplanner.ScreenFunc`, `intaketriage.Actor`/`ErrAIActorForbidden`, `aiprovenance.NewAIWithOpts`/`NewHuman`, `coverage.SourceCoverage.Cursor`.
- Honest non-guarantees: `ResumeFSM` doc must state history-since-resume only (no replay) and that terminal-state hydration is for read/guard use; `ClampToCeiling` doc must state it does not retro-fix stored assessments.

## Non-goals & theater traps

- Do NOT rebuild `intake-triage` or `query-planner` — kit sides exist and are tested (`foundations/review/intake-triage`, `foundations/investigation/query-planner`). D35-1/D35-2 work is adoption + deletion, plus the one `ResumeFSM` seam.
- Do NOT route `ExcludeRecord`/`RestoreRecord` through the FSM or bolt an `ai:` guard onto them — they are record-exclusion registry writes with no guard today; forcing them into proposal triage is a wrong refactor, and a new guard there is new behavior needing its own decision.
- Do NOT port PKCE, loopback listener, token-endpoint HTTP, or file-backed `TokenStore` into the kit — doc-35 §3 explicitly scopes those as adapter work, and file I/O would violate foundation norms.
- Do NOT move `ScoreRelevance` to the kit (different concern; single consumer; would reopen amendment 2).
- Do NOT add checkpoint semantics to `coverage` beyond the doc paragraph — the field already exists; adding a parallel API is the theater version of "folding".
- Do NOT touch throughline's ~120 dirty files beyond the declared scope (target-file disjointness check in Write scope); the sole sanctioned collision is the `go mod vendor` re-sync, which must be diffed and attributed per the Stage 2 deliverable.
- Theater traps: marking D35-1/D35-2 `[x]` with the kit package tested but the donor still compiled in throughline (the exact state the rows are stuck in today); silently changing `planner_test.go` expectations to match kit output instead of proving parity; smuggling assertion edits into `service_test.go` as "plumbing" (only the itemized forbidden-transition list is allowed); a `tokenlifecycle` that re-implements `TokenStatus` but throughline keeps its own copy "for safety"; clamping inside `Assess` (silent behavior change to a shipped pure function); ticking the TRACKING "donor NOT deleted" removal without the donor actually deleted. Overclaiming any of these = defect class equal to a failing test (VISION.md).
